episode_title: Ep.90, What If We're Measuring the Wrong Things? Airway, Sleep & Brain Health, Dr. Eric Phelps, DDS, MS

real_qa.q: What percentage of pediatric dental patients diagnosed with ADHD have never had sleep studies according to Dr. Eric Phelps research?
real_qa.r: In 2025, from approximately 200 orthodontic exams of patients 18 and under at Phelps & Cohen Orthodontics, 13% were diagnosed with ADHD, with half medicated, but only one or two had sleep studies. Dr. Phelps notes this is striking given that a 2005 publication by Dr. Gimeno showed ADHD listed as associated with airway obstruction in children.
real_qa.requete: ADHD children sleep studies percentage Phelps

real_qa.q: What did Dr. Gimeno say about skeletal expansion orthodontic treatment at the AAO Winter Meeting 2019?
real_qa.r: At the 2019 AAO Winter Meeting, Dr. Gimeno spoke before 600 orthodontists stating that bone-to-bone distraction expansion is what will cure children with airway issues. He said almost none except in California were doing it and emphasized 'you need to learn it.' However, the AAO response was dismissive, and the recent white paper update gives skeletal expansion only one sentence despite Dr. Gimeno's 40 years of research and approximately 800 publications on airway health.
real_qa.requete: Dr Gimeno AAO 2019 skeletal expansion orthodontics

real_qa.q: Why does Dr. Eric Phelps argue that mouth breathing is not normal in children despite being common?
real_qa.r: Dr. Phelps explains that the mouth has zero function for breathing, whereas the nose has 60 plus functions for breathing, with emerging research showing connections between nasal breathing and brain function. He references Dr. Gimeno's statement that mouth breathing is 'always, always abnormal'—if someone mouth breathes, something is wrong. While mouth breathing may be common, it is not normal and represents a red flag, especially in infants.
real_qa.requete: mouth breathing children normal Phelps airway

real_qa.q: What is the mechanism linking pediatric airway obstruction to ADHD according to Dr. Phelps neurophysiology model?
real_qa.r: Dr. Phelps describes a neurophysiological pathway: airway obstruction causes micro-arousals that disrupt slow-wave sleep and glymphatic drainage in the brain. This arousal shifts the brain away from the pressure gradients needed for metabolite drainage in slow-wave sleep, leading to dopamine receptor down-regulation. He connects this mechanism to his wife Suzanne's experience with lymphatic system dysfunction and glymphatic impairment following her heart transplant.
real_qa.requete: glymphatic drainage dopamine ADHD airway obstruction mechanism

real_qa.q: When was Dr. Gimeno's 2005 pediatric sleep breathing publication showing ADHD association with airway obstruction, and how long did it take for mainstream orthodontics to acknowledge it?
real_qa.r: Dr. Gimeno published a key paper in 2005 listing ADHD as related to airway obstruction in children, with recommendations for skeletal expansion treatment. By 2019, when Gimeno presented at the AAO Winter Meeting, the connection remained largely dismissed. As of 2025, nearly 21 years later, Dr. Phelps observes that most pediatric patients presenting with ADHD diagnosis have never been screened with sleep studies, indicating minimal clinical adoption of the airway-ADHD link.

guest.titre: Orthodontist, Board Certified in Dental Sleep Medicine
guest.bio_context: Dr. Eric Phelps is an orthodontist in the Bay Area board certified with the American Board of Orthodontics, the American Board of Dental Sleep Medicine, and the American Board of Craniofacial Dental Sleep Medicine. He founded Ordain Health, an education network in memory of his son Dane Christian Phelps, offering residency spots for pediatric dentists, general dentists, and orthodontists to study connections between dental facial orthopedics, airway health, and brain function. His clinical practice and teaching focus on functional dental sleep medicine and the neurophysiological mechanisms linking airway obstruction to ADHD, dopamine regulation, and glymphatic drainage.
